description: Composite group of three images: a full-width data table at the top and two horizontal bar charts, (a) and (b), stacked below it. The table is headed "Nominal alloy composition (at.%)" and lists the two binaries plus nine alloyed compositions with columns "Fe–Al Matrix" — "Grains" (Morphology, Size (μm)) and "Dendrites" (Morphology, Size (μm)) — and "Precipitates" (Chemical formula, Morphology, Size (μm)). Printed entries include polygonal 500 μm grains for Fe–15Al and 700 μm for Fe–26Al, columnar 350×2000 μm (Fe–15Al–2V–1C) and 450×3000 μm (Fe–26Al–2V–1C), and TiC/VC/NbC/TaC precipitates described as fibrous, lamellar, granular, plate-like (needle-like), cube-like and script-like, 0.5–5 μm, with two "<1" entries. Charts (a) and (b) share a 0–1100 x-axis with 100-unit ticks and the legend grey = "Yield stress in compression [MPa]", light grey = "Hardness of matrix [HB]"; no value labels are printed on the bars. (a) ranks Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C; (b) ranks Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C. The pairing argues that Ti/V/Nb/Ta carbide additions strengthen Fe–15Al alloys but that Ti additions soften Fe–26Al alloys.

observations.observation: The figure group is composite: a data table on top and two horizontal bar charts labelled (a) and (b) below it.
Both bar charts share an x-axis from 0 to 1100 with ticks every 100 units and a legend where dark grey = 'Yield stress in compression [MPa]' and light grey = 'Hardness of matrix [HB]'.
No numeric value labels are printed on any bar; values can only be read against the axis ticks.

In panel (a) the yield-stress bars of Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C and Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C extend past the 800 tick and are much longer than those of Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C and Fe-15Al-2V-1C, whose bars fall between the 300 and 500 ticks.
In panel (a) the hardness bars of Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C and Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C reach around the 300 tick, whereas Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C and Fe-15Al-2V-1C lie between the 100 and 200 ticks.

In panel (b) Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C has the longest yield-stress bar (approaching the 800 tick), Fe-26Al the second longest (between the 600 and 700 ticks), and Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C and Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C the shortest (between the 400 and 500 ticks).

In panel (b) the hardness bars of all Fe-26Al-based alloys cluster between roughly the 200 and 300 ticks, so the hardness differences between them are small compared with the yield-stress differences.
The table states grain morphology/size: polygonal 500 μm for Fe-15Al, polygonal 700 μm for Fe-26Al, columnar 350×2000 μm for Fe-15Al-2V-1C and columnar 450×3000 μm for Fe-26Al-2V-1C.
The table states dendritic morphology 'Equiaxed and columnar' with size '30, 30×80' for Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C and Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C.

The precipitate phases listed in the table are TiC, VC, NbC, TaC and, for Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, 'NbC and (Fe, Al)₂Nb', with morphologies including fibrous, lamellar (in eutectic), plate-like (needle-like), granular, cube-like and script-like.

The caption states that Fig. 1 shows the yield stress in compression and the Brinell hardness of the matrix at room temperature for Fe–15Al-based (a) and Fe–26Al-based (b) alloys, and that the upper table gives the microstructure characterisation of the investigated alloys.
The citing text states that all Fe–15Al–2M–1C alloys exhibit strengthening of the Fe–Al matrix in comparison with the binary Fe–15Al alloy.
The citing text states that the alloys with V, Nb or Ta show higher hardness than the binary Fe–26Al alloy, whereas the alloys containing Ti are softened.

The citing text states that the alloy Fe–15Al–2Nb–1C has higher hardness but lower yield stress than Fe–15Al–2Ta–1C, and that except for Fe–26Al–4Nb–1C all Fe–26Al-based alloys exhibit lower compressive yield stress than the binary Fe–26Al alloy.

subfigures.description: Full-width table titled 'Nominal alloy composition (at.%)' with sub-headers Fe–Al Matrix (Grains: Morphology, Size (μm); Dendrites: Morphology, Size (μm)) and Precipitates (Chemical formula, Morphology, Size (μm)); 11 rows covering Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C, Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C, with grain/dendrite morphologies and precipitate phases (TiC, VC, NbC, TaC, NbC and (Fe, Al)₂Nb) and sizes.

Horizontal grouped bar chart for Fe–15Al-based alloys (Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C) with x-axis 0–1100 (100-unit ticks); dark grey bars = yield stress in compression [MPa], light grey bars = hardness of matrix [HB]. The two Ta/Nb-containing alloys show by far the longest yield-stress bars (beyond the 800 tick), while Fe-15Al is shortest.

Horizontal grouped bar chart for Fe–26Al-based alloys (Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C) on the same 0–1100 axis and legend. Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C has the longest yield-stress bar (near 800), Fe-26Al the next longest, and the two Ti-containing alloys the shortest, while their hardness bars are all similar (between the 200 and 300 ticks).
